title: Use analyzers and the portal · Level 3
slo: Choose and test an analyzer for a common extraction task.

exercises.question_text: What does a confidence score show for an extracted field value?

options.rationale: A confidence score indicates service certainty in an extracted value. It expresses confidence for that result.
An analyzer ID identifies the analyzer used. It does not measure certainty.
options.better_fit: Use this when identifying the producing analyzer.

options.text: How text is arranged on a page
options.rationale: Text layout describes page arrangement. Confidence measures value certainty.
options.better_fit: Use this when reviewing document layout.

options.rationale: A schema defines fields before analysis. Confidence is returned for extracted values.
options.better_fit: Use this when describing extraction requirements.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Confidence measures service certainty in an extracted value.

exercises.question_text: What can you do in the Foundry portal? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The portal accepts uploaded material for testing. This supports validation before automation.

options.text: Run an analyzer on a media file
options.rationale: The portal can select source media and run an analyzer. It supports testing media inputs.
The portal can display returned JSON. This helps review structured output.
Polling belongs to asynchronous API workflows. It is not a stated portal-testing action.
options.better_fit: Use this in code after an asynchronous API request.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The portal can upload content, run analysis, and show JSON.

exercises.question_text: An analyzer supplied for a common scenario is a ___.

parts.text: An analyzer supplied for a common scenario is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A tailored option could be confused with a supplied one.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use prebuilt for a ready common-scenario analyzer.

exercises.explanation: A prebuilt analyzer is supplied for a common scenario.

exercises.question_text: Which are roles of an analyzer? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: An analyzer applies AI analysis to submitted content. This is its central role.
Analyzers return structured results. Those results support later workflows.
A configured analyzer reuses its extraction logic and schema. This makes output predictable.

options.text: Creates a new schema for every request
options.rationale: Analyzers reuse their configured schema for similar inputs. New schemas per request reduce consistency.
options.better_fit: This may be needed when requirements genuinely change.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Analyzers analyze input, return structured results, and reuse configured logic.

exercises.question_text: The Foundry portal can test an analyzer only after the workflow is automated in code.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An application could be built without checking returned fields.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use the portal to test uploads before automating extraction.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Portal testing occurs before code automation.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the steps for reusing one analyzer on a submitted receipt.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A result would be placed before the analysis that produces it.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Follow the dependency from analyzer selection through returned JSON.

exercises.correct_answer: Choose analyzer Submit receipt Apply configured schema Receive structured JSON
exercises.explanation: Select the analyzer, submit content, apply its schema, then receive structured JSON.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the phrase that distinguishes a custom analyzer.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The custom-versus-prebuilt distinction would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Keep the tailoring relationship together in the completed statement.

exercises.correct_answer: A custom analyzer is tailored to your extraction requirements and schema
exercises.explanation: Custom analyzers are tailored to a user's extraction requirements and schema.

exercises.question_text: What does text layout information describe?

options.text: How text is arranged on a page
options.rationale: Text layout describes the arrangement of text on a page. It helps identify where content appears.

options.text: How confident a field value is
options.rationale: Confidence measures certainty in an extracted value. It does not describe page arrangement.
options.better_fit: Use this when interpreting a confidence score.

options.rationale: An analyzer ID identifies the analyzer used. Layout describes text placement.
options.better_fit: Use this when identifying an analyzer ID.

options.text: How an audio call was spoken
options.rationale: Speech concerns audio analysis. Text layout concerns document pages.
options.better_fit: Use this when discussing an audio recording.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Layout information describes page text arrangement.

exercises.question_text: The reusable configuration that specifies which fields an analyzer should extract is a ___.

parts.text: The reusable configuration that specifies which fields an analyzer should extract is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The requested field structure would remain undefined.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A schema defines fields; an analyzer performs analysis.

exercises.explanation: A schema specifies fields and structure for extraction.

exercises.question_text: An inspection manager needs fields that no supplied analyzer covers for paper safety forms. Which choices should the manager make? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The fields are organization-specific and uncovered. A custom analyzer can be tailored for them.

options.text: Define the required inspection fields in a schema
options.rationale: The tailored extraction needs a defined field structure. A schema supplies that definition.
An invoice analyzer targets a different common scenario. It will not match unique safety-form fields.
options.better_fit: Use this for standard invoices that fit its extraction.

feedback.intrinsic: Important safety fields may not be returned.
feedback.instructional: Unique uncovered fields indicate a custom analyzer and schema.

options.rationale: The input is paper forms, not video. The required fields are also unique.
options.better_fit: Use this for a suitable video-analysis scenario.

feedback.intrinsic: An unrelated analyzer would be selected.
feedback.instructional: Evaluate both content type and required fields.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Unique uncovered fields require a custom analyzer and schema.

exercises.question_text: The portal can map a field such as Vendor address to its extracted value.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The link between a field and its value could be missed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Document analysis can map fields such as Vendor address to extracted values.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A result can show a field and its mapped value.

exercises.question_text: Which details can an extraction result include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: An extraction result can include an analyzer ID. It identifies the analyzer used.
An extraction result can include API-version metadata. It is a returned result detail.
Returned fields can include data types such as string or date. These help interpret values.
Configuration is created before analysis. It is not returned result metadata.
options.better_fit: Use this when creating or tailoring an analyzer.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Results can include metadata and typed field details.
